requirements.requirement: On node1, set the persistent system hostname to os-lab.infra.test.
requirements.summary: The runtime hostname, static hostname, and /etc/hostname all had the exact requested value before restart. After an acknowledged restart and verified boot-ID change, all three still had that value, directly demonstrating persistence.

requirements.requirement: Ensure node1 can resolve os-lab.infra.test locally.
requirements.summary: /etc/hosts maps os-lab.infra.test to 127.0.1.1, and getent returned that address both before and after the verified restart.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-restart evidence. The restart protocol records the pre-restart boot identity and working task state, restart scheduling, a different post-restart boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovery of hostname, resolver mapping, and multi-user.target. The persistent pre-existing SSH failure does not affect the task result or hygiene assessment.
limitations: The provider-wide restart evidence cannot demonstrate a wholly healthy systemd state because ssh.service was failed both before and after execution. Baseline evidence establishes that this condition pre-existed the executor; task-specific functionality and multi-user.target nevertheless recovered successfully (global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services, global:after_executor:node1:failed-services, cmd-a483e043cbb74559).

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified, so none remained or required reversion. Setting the hostname was required (cmd-5b4d899d51c04c70), replacing the 127.0.1.1 hosts entry directly established local resolution (cmd-1db7ae7238d749d4), and scheduling one bounded reboot supported mandatory restart evidence and persistence verification (cmd-b0f4aa1e74384f9b). Other commands were read-only validation or reboot polling. The failed ssh.service existed at baseline and remained unchanged, while package health remained intact; it is therefore not executor-caused residue.
